name: Cai

attributes.attribute: an Irish brehon, a judge of the early law
a Milesian who studied the law of Moses in Egypt
in the Arthurian line the hero Kay of the court
the Welsh form of the Arthurian Kay
close to Arthur in the tale Pa Gur and in Culhwch and Obwen
fights witches and monsters and can last nine days in water

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cai is a variant spelling of the Welsh hero named Cei. He rides with King Arthur and the good Bedwyr. Cai holds the post of seneschal to the royal court. His temper blends bold courage with plain jest. The Black Book of Carmarthen hails him a hero. That twelfth-century book prints his brave deed. Later stories turn Cai into a cross house steward. That steward shows cruel and silly habits. The same Latin name also marks an Irish judge. That judge of the Milesians read Moses' law while in Egypt. The separate figures stay apart in the first books. The Latin root Caius unites the shared names. The knight Sir Kay springs from this older man.

okr.objective: Cai is a hero and judge shared with the name Cei.
